title: AAA 1 - How to Soak in Programming Concepts and more...
summary: First Ask-Me-Anything session (recorded for an earlier iOS course), answering general learner questions on how to absorb programming knowledge, getting a first dev job, studying, learning new tech, focus and daily routines. Nothing technical to build.

concepts.heading: Learning and skill building
points: Learn fundamentals first and surface features last; treat knowledge as a tree so flashy details have something to attach to.
Build your own small projects. Keep each one a minimal working version, then add features one at a time. Over-ambitious first projects tend to be abandoned.
Skills transfer between languages (variables, data types, functions), so a new language mostly means new syntax.
Searching well (Google, Stack Overflow, official docs) is a core professional skill; looking things up is normal.
When learning something new, map it onto what you already know, and schedule regular time for work outside your comfort zone.

concepts.heading: Career and study advice
points: Without a portfolio, start on freelance marketplaces (Upwork, Fiverr and similar) to get real clients, real requirements and reviews; pay is low at first but raises as the track record grows.
At university prefer breadth and connections over chasing perfect grades.
Bias is not something you control; focus on factors you can change such as preparation, portfolio and work ethic.

concepts.heading: Focus and routine
points: Protect attention: turn off notifications, and disconnect from the internet when it is not needed.
Reduce small daily decisions (clothes, breakfast) to save mental energy for work.
Her routine: short exercise, 20 minutes of meditation, journaling, then skimming tech news. Don't worry about missing days.
